claims.explanation: Quisinostat is a pan-HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on class I HDAC activity and intact apoptotic signaling, with TP53 loss and RAS/BRAF pathway activation marking sensitive lineages. The strongest recurrent pattern is TP53 mutation in nearly all selectively killed lines, consistent with HDAC inhibitor-induced DNA damage and apoptosis requiring p53-independent mitotic/mitochondrial death in p53-deficient tumors, while wild-type or functionally intact p53 lines are less affected. Additional sensitizing features include BRAF/NRAS/MAPK activation and ARID1A loss, whereas protective features include intact p53 pathway and possibly EGFR/MAP2K1-driven survival signaling.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in almost all selectively killed lines and absent in most least-affected lines; p53-deficient cells may rely on HDAC-dependent survival and undergo mitotic catastrophe/apoptos
BRAF mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (8305C, SH4, SNUC5, UACC62) and BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid/colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
NRAS mutations in sensitive lines (SW1088, IPC298) suggest MAPK pathway activation sensitizes to HDAC inhibition
ARID1A loss occurs in several sensitive lines (SNUC5, EFE184, HS766T, SW1088) and may impair chromatin remodeling, enhancing HDAC inhibitor effects
KRAS mutations in sensitive lines (HS766T, NCIH1792, LS1034) suggest oncogenic RAS signaling contributes to sensitivity
CDKN2A loss in several sensitive lines (8305C, HS766T, YD10B, IPC298) may release cell-cycle checkpoints, increasing HDAC inhibitor-induced death
EGFR-mutant lines NCIH1650 and KYSE270 are sensitive, but EGFR-mutant KNS81 and NCIH1437 are resistant, suggesting EGFR mutation alone is not sensitizing and may be protective in some contexts
MAP2K1 mutation in resistant line NCIH1437 suggests MEK/ERK activation can protect from HDAC inhibitor-induced apoptosis
PTEN mutation in resistant lines TE4 and ZR751 suggests PI3K/AKT survival signaling protects against HDAC inhibition
SMARCA4 mutation in resistant lines SKNSH, OV7, and KYSE270 (sensitive) is mixed, but SMARCA4 loss may reduce chromatin accessibility needed for HDAC inhibitor response
JNJ-26481585 was selected for prolonged HDAC1 inhibition, so high HDAC1 expression may predict greater target engagement and sensitivity
MDM2 is a secondary target; MDM2 overexpression may reduce p53-independent apoptosis and protect cells from HDAC inhibitor-induced death
